scope: Canonical data/validation, history metadata and synthetic persistence only; no restore execution/live tests

checks.name: App release build and three Worker dry builds
Changed prose, whitespace and document validation

acceptance_evidence: Twenty-six neutral valid/invalid documents agree across C# and the pinned Workers runtime, including causal overlap, exact references, command roles, archive retention, UTC/default times and revision bounds.

Optional restoration records retain old completions. Successive Todo completions require a unique intervening restoration; tasks with restoration history match the latest cycle. Daily occurrence uniqueness remains unchanged.
Absent/null extensions retain legacy serialized defaults, explicit empty extensions remain explicit and existing active-history acceptance remains compatible.
Current Todo state drives goal progress; repeated history does not inflate counts. Archived records retain causal meaning and wall-clock skew does not override causal revision.
Completing a restored Todo adds a new completion and preserves prior cycles, journal validity and original command duplication behavior.
History exposes explicit restoration metadata and omits the extension on ordinary rows. Backup restore and frozen handoff retain all cycle data.
The standalone Worker fixture denies all outbound calls and records zero attempts.
limitations: The model does not expose a restore execution tool; T-bc51e9bd-b06f-494a-b1d3-bdc7c4a5f23f remains required.
Strict clients without extension support require coordinated updates before using restoration data. No automatic migration tooling or reward reversal is supplied.
Production UI, real host/device behavior and live qualification remain unrun.
